 RULEMAKING TO UPDATE                            §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 WHOLESALE AND IOU RETAIL                        §
 TRANSMISSION COST RECOVERY                      §
 IN THE ERCOT REGION 9                           §                    OF TEXAS

FREEPORT LNG DEVELOPMENT, L.P. COMMENTS TO STAFF’S PROPOSAL FOR
            PUBLICATION AND REQUEST FOR COMMENTS

                                      I.   INTRODUCTION

Freeport LNG Development, L.P. (“Freeport LNG”) appreciates the opportunity to comment on
the proposal for publication in Project No. 58000.



                                II.    ABOUT FREEPORT LNG

Freeport LNG is an LNG export company headquartered in Houston, Texas. The company' s three-
train, 17 MTPA natural gas liquefaction facility is the largest all-electric drive liquefied natural
gas (LNG) facility in the world, making it the most environmentally sustainable site of its kind.
The facility' s electric drive motors reduce carbon emissions by over 90% relative to gas turbine-
driven liquefaction facilities. Freeport LNG was formed in 2002 to develop, own and operate an
LNG terminal on Quintana Island, near Freeport, Texas. The terminal started LNG import
operations in June 2008 and began LNG export operations in 2019.

Freeport LNG's operations indirectly support more than 30,000 jobs, primarily in Texas, as a result
of incremental natural gas exploration, production, and processing associated with the LNG
produced and exported by its facilities. These LNG exports have a $5 to 7 billion net positive
impact to the U.S. economy each year. Locally, Freeport LNG is estimated to pay over $2.6 billion
in taxes to local taxing jurisdictions over its facility's 20-year initial operating life.

Since its founding in 2002, Freeport LNG has remained committed to corporate philanthropy and
being a steadfast supporter of the communities in which we operate. Freeport LNG is an integral
part of Brazoria County communities while employing over 350 full-time employees in Brazoria
County. Additionally, it is estimated that Freeport LNG's activities contributed almost $640
million, directly and indirectly, to the Brazoria County economy in 2024 alone, as well as
supported almost 1,100 jobs in the county and provided $26.5 million in revenues for local taxing
jurisdictions in the same year.




                                                 1
                             III.    FREEPORT LNG COMMENTS

Freeport LNG supports the Commission's objective of ensuring that transmission costs are
appropriately assigned and that customers reserving significant transmission capacity provide
reasonable assurances that transmission investments will be utilized. However, the proposed
framework appears primarily designed to address the risks associated with large speculative
computational loads and will unintentionally capture existing and expanding traditional industrial
facilities, like Freeport LNG, that present fundamentally different development, investment, and
operating characteristics. LNG export facilities and other long-lived industrial projects require
substantial fixed capital investment, extensive permitting, site-specific infrastructure, long
development timelines, and multi-decade operating commitments that materially reduce the risk
of stranded transmission investment.

Freeport LNG suggests consideration of the following:

      Ensure that existing industrial facilities and traditional industrial expansions are not subject
       to the same requirements as speculative large-load developments solely due to their size.
       Existing industrial facilities present materially different development, investment, and
       operating characteristics than speculative load developments.
      Consider factors beyond demand size when applying large-load requirements and establish
       an alternative compliance framework for traditional industrial facilities that can
       demonstrate substantial fixed capital investment, long-term operating commitments, site-
       specific infrastructure, and a long-term commitment to operations in Texas.
      Provide grandfathering provisions or alternative treatment for expansions of existing
       industrial facilities that have established operating histories, existing transmission
       investments, and demonstrated long-term commitments to Texas.
      Recognize objective evidence of project commitment, including Final Investment
       Decisions (FID), execution of Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC)
       contracts, obtaining debt and/or equity commitments for the project, substantial
       engineering, procurement and/or construction activities, interconnection security postings,
       and energization milestones, as alternative demonstrations of project viability when
       evaluating minimum demand obligations, financial commitments, and long-term
       transmission reservation requirements.
      Support a transmission cost allocation framework grounded in cost-causation principles,
       including appropriate weighting of monthly coincident peaks so that periods driving
       transmission investment and reliability needs are reflected proportionally in customer cost
       responsibility.

The following comments provide additional detail and supporting rationale for each of the
recommendations summarized above.

Applicability of the Large Load Framework to Existing Industrial Facilities

Freeport LNG is an existing large industrial load that has operated in ERCOT for many years, has
made substantial investments in Texas, and is evaluating future facility expansions that would
build upon existing operations, infrastructure, and transmission service. As a result, Freeport LNG

                                                  2
 believes the proposed framework does not sufficiently distinguish between existing industrial
facilities pursuing incremental expansion and new large-load developments whose ultimate level
of load materialization remains uncertain.

Freeport LNG supports the Commission's objective of ensuring that transmission investments are
prudently planned and appropriately utilized. However, the proposed requirements would apply
the same minimum billing demand obligations, reservation requirements, and long-term
commitments to existing industrial facilities expanding established operations as they would to
entirely new large-load developments. Freeport LNG believes these scenarios present materially
different levels of risk and should be evaluated accordingly. Existing industrial facilities have
already demonstrated a long-term commitment to Texas through years of successful operations,
continued investment, existing transmission service, employment, and substantial contributions to
local communities and taxing jurisdictions.

Demand Size Alone Does Not Reflect Project Risk

Freeport LNG suggests that factors beyond demand size be considered when evaluating the
applicability of minimum demand commitments and long-term reservation requirements. While
demand size may be an administratively simple screening criterion, it does not adequately
distinguish between fundamentally different categories of customers.

As an existing LNG export facility, Freeport LNG's future load growth would be supported by
significant capital commitments, years of engineering and development work, extensive permitting
requirements, major construction activities, significant debt and equity commitments, and long-
term commercial arrangements. These characteristics differ materially from projects that may seek
large amounts of transmission capacity before committing comparable levels of capital and
infrastructure investment. Freeport LNG believes that project readiness, financial commitment,
and demonstrated operational history are more meaningful indicators of transmission planning risk
than demand size alone.

Establish a Qualified Traditional Industrial Load Exemption

Freeport LNG recommends consideration of an exemption or alternative compliance framework
for traditional industrial facilities that can demonstrate substantial, long-term commitments to
operations within Texas. Freeport LNG suggests that qualification for such treatment could be
demonstrated through various objective factors including:

      Significant fixed capital investment;
      Existing operating facilities;
      Long-term operating permits;
      Site-specific infrastructure that cannot reasonably be relocated;
      Long-term commitments to operations within Texas; and/or
      Existing economic contributions to local communities and taxing jurisdictions.




                                               3
 Freeport LNG believes these factors provide strong evidence that future load growth associated
with existing industrial facilities will materialize and therefore warrant consideration under a
framework that appropriately reflects the lower stranded-cost risk associated with such projects.

Treatment of Existing Industrial Facility Expansions

Freeport LNG recommends that the Commission consider grandfathering provisions or alternative
treatment for expansions of existing industrial facilities that have already demonstrated long-term
utilization of transmission infrastructure and substantial investment within Texas.

Freeport LNG believes there is an important distinction between a new large-load development
and the expansion of an existing industrial facility. Existing facilities have established operating
histories, demonstrated demand for transmission service, and proven long-term commitments to
their Texas locations.

Future expansions of Freeport LNG would represent incremental growth of an existing operating
facility rather than a speculative development of a completely new industrial site. The transmission
planning risks associated with these types of expansions are materially different than those
associated with undeveloped projects that have not yet demonstrated a comparable level of
commitment or operational history.

Alternative to the Proposed 20-Year Minimum Billing Obligation

Freeport LNG understands the Commission's objective of ensuring that transmission capacity
reserved for large-load customers ultimately results in actual load growth and utilization of the
electric system. However, for existing industrial facilities pursuing expansion projects, Freeport
LNG respectfully suggests that objective project-development milestones may provide a more
direct demonstration of commitment than a blanket twenty-year minimum demand obligation.

For major industrial projects, meaningful commitment is often demonstrated long before a facility
consumes its first megawatt of electricity. Freeport LNG recommends that the Commission
consider recognizing objective milestones such as:

      Final Investment Decision (FID);
      Execution of EPC contracts;
      Debt and/or equity commitments to the project;
      Commencement of major engineering, procurement and/or construction activities;
      Posting of interconnection security; and/or
      Achievement of energization milestones.

These milestones require substantial financial commitments and represent significant project
advancement. Meeting several of these milestones provides tangible evidence that the project is
moving toward completion and eventual utilization of the requested transmission capacity.

For existing industrial facilities that have already demonstrated a long-term commitment to Texas
and subsequently achieve these development milestones, Freeport LNG believes there is a strong
